title: To achieve its next economic leap, Vietnam needs to move beyond the factory floor
gist: Amin Mohseni-Cheraghlou argues Vietnam's FDI-driven export model (2025 exports $475bn, record $27.6bn FDI disbursements) is capturing too little domestic value: foreign firms make 77% of exports and grew 26.1% while domestic exporters fell 6.1%. With deep US-China exposure, tightening rules of origin, aging demographics and a swing to a $15bn H1 2026 trade deficit on Iran-war fuel prices, Vietnam must move from 'China plus one' to 'Vietnam plus value' via semis, suppliers, digital and green energy.

insights.claim: Vietnam's economy has grown nearly fivefold since 2000, and merchandise exports reached $475 billion in 2025, almost four times 2010 levels, with manufactured goods nearly 89 percent.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Confirms Vietnam as a top-tier Asian manufacturing hub.
insights.quote: Merchandise exports reached $475 billion in 2025, almost four times their level in 2010, with manufactured goods accounting for nearly 89 percent.

insights.claim: Vietnam's FDI disbursements hit a record $27.6 billion in 2025, nearly 10 percent higher than in 2024.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Investor confidence in Vietnam remains strong despite trade-policy risk.

themes.theme: Dual economy: foreign vs. domestic firms

insights.claim: Foreign-invested firms made 77 percent of Vietnam's 2025 merchandise exports; their exports surged 26.1 percent while domestic firms' exports fell 6.1 percent.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Export growth headlines mask weak domestic corporate earnings capture.
insights.quote: exports by domestic firms fell 6.1 percent, while those of foreign-invested firms surged 26.1 percent

insights.claim: The World Bank estimates value added per worker in Vietnamese domestic private firms is only about one-fifth that of foreign-invested firms.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Large productivity gap is both risk and upside for domestic equities if linkages improve.

insights.claim: Vietnam's challenge is no longer attracting FDI but converting it into domestic productivity via supplier development, tech and skills transfer.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Policy will tilt toward local-content and supplier-linkage incentives.

insights.claim: The biggest payoff from future FDI may come not from attracting another multinational but from connecting Vietnamese companies to MNCs already there.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Domestic suppliers to MNC supply chains are the investable beneficiaries.
insights.quote: The biggest economic payoff from future FDI may come not from attracting another MNC, but from connecting Vietnamese companies to the MNCs already investing there.
insights.locator: Domestic suppliers: The biggest economic payoff

insights.claim: Vietnam's population is aging, and the IMF expects demographic change to weigh on medium-term potential growth, so growth must come from output per worker.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Labor-cost advantage will erode; productivity is the key growth variable.
insights.locator: Demographics make that transition more urgent.

themes.theme: US-China squeeze and rules of origin

insights.claim: In 2025 the US bought $153.2 billion of Vietnamese goods, about one-third of exports, while China supplied $186 billion of Vietnam's imports.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Vietnam is a transshipment-style node exposed to both sides of US-China tensions.

insights.claim: The IMF estimates value added in Vietnamese exports ultimately destined for the US equals 10 percent of GDP, one of Asia's highest exposures.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: US tariff decisions are a first-order macro risk for Vietnam.
insights.quote: value added embedded in exports ultimately destined for the United States was equivalent to 10 percent of Vietnam’s GDP

insights.claim: US trade policy's growing focus on Chinese content and rules of origin, not just assembly location, undermines Vietnam's role as a final-assembly alternative to China.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: 'China plus one' assembly plays face rising tariff and compliance risk.

insights.claim: Vietnam's trade balance swung to an estimated $15 billion deficit in H1 2026 from a $7.6 billion surplus a year earlier, driven largely by surging fuel prices amid the Iran war.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: External balance deterioration is a pressure point for the dong and reserves.
